built.label: real

learnings.claim: On the AMD iGPU the page's wide shots are fill-bound. Drawing 60 % fewer triangles left fps unchanged; half the pixels doubled it. Only resolution and MSAA moved 1080p by more than noise, and VSM shadows cost 51 %.
learnings.surprise: Mesh reduction was expected to buy frame rate; it pays only after fill cost is cut.

learnings.claim: Iteration time on an agent-made video goes to agent build and tooling, not rendering. Of 1,446 logged minutes, rendering was 54. In drafts 9-11, each stage took 20-60 min of subagent build against ~3 min of rendering.
learnings.surprise: Rendering was treated as the bottleneck (render-fps.md was opened for it). The timelog moved the effort to changed-scene diffs, the scene cache and numeric stills checks.

learnings.claim: An agent's knot claim checked only on stills was wrong for four drafts. The closing half hitches were tucked under their own leg, which makes no knot, through drafts 9-12. Checking against NASA Fig. 9-3 and a slid-off knot determinant caught it.
learnings.surprise: Stills review by an agent was taken as verification of topology.

learnings.claim: Turning stills-round judgements into numeric test rules (an anchor on a drawn strand, a knot's projected px, a card's coverage) replaced most screenshot rounds; `--only stills` runs in 2.6 s with no browser.

A per-scene render cache keyed on what each scene reads, plus a multi-slot GPU render server, took a full 4,133-frame draft from 394-517 s cold on one iGPU browser to 141.9 s on 7 RTX 3090 slots. A one-scene review takes ~112 s, a warm re-render 3.5 s.
learnings.surprise: render-fps.md D2 decided to stay on the iGPU and not try the 3090 (render-fps.md:144). The render server reversed that in practice, and the doc still says D2.

learnings.claim: Agents waiting on long jobs with foreground poll loops wasted 203 min across 5 sessions (166 loops). fab perf still lists polling as the top waste in this repo's longest sessions (1.8 h, 1.5 h). The rule is now run_in_background plus a lock that queues.

Two sessions editing the same files in one checkout forced hunk-by-hunk staging. A worktree per session fixes it, at the cost of linking git-ignored parts/ and .cache/. Draft 15 then hit worktree-only test failures from CRLF checkout and junctions.

Building a feature on a parent repo's model without checking the parent let the fork drift onto a deleted design. Upstream replaced the static cord route with a rope simulation 1-4 days after the fork point. The lacing was built 2026-11-08 on the static route, and nothing in the fork's docs records upstream's state.
learnings.surprise: The fork's docs treat lr4.py's cord_route as the live twin to keep in step; upstream deleted it in Part 53c.

learnings.claim: Generating the whole knotted run on a body beat splicing knots into a precomputed run. The splice showed kinks and gaps; the maintainer chose the generic rope path, which is draft 15.
learnings.surprise: The splice (d14) was the first, cheaper-looking route.
